scr_ar_posted_payment_page.purpose: The posted payment record page showing payer, date, method, reference, deposit, and the invoices and credits the payment was applied to.
scr_ar_posted_payment_page.outcome: A complete view of one customer receipt for review, disputes and audit samples.
scr_ar_posted_payment_page.rootCause: Auditors testing cash receipts and customers disputing balances both need to see exactly how a receipt was recorded and applied; this page is that evidence.
scr_ar_posted_payment_page.ifSkipped: Receipt questions cannot be answered from the system and disputes drag on.

scr_ar_printing_posted_payment_details.purpose: Prints the details of a posted customer payment — for example to send a commercial tenant confirmation of how their check was applied.
scr_ar_printing_posted_payment_details.outcome: A document confirming receipt and application for the customer or file.
scr_ar_printing_posted_payment_details.rootCause: Tenants and affiliates often dispute how payments were applied; a printed application record resolves those disputes quickly.
scr_ar_printing_posted_payment_details.ifSkipped: Application disputes take longer to resolve and payments are withheld meanwhile.
redFlags: Payment confirmations sent to unverified contacts

scr_ar_writing_off_unpaid_invoices.purpose: Writes off unpaid A/R invoices judged uncollectible — for example a former retail tenant that closed owing rent — through an adjustment against the allowance or bad debt expense.
scr_ar_writing_off_unpaid_invoices.outcome: Uncollectible receivables are removed and the loss recognized, with the invoice and adjustment linked.
scr_ar_writing_off_unpaid_invoices.rootCause: Carrying uncollectible balances overstates assets; GAAP requires receivables at the amount expected to be collected. Write-offs must be approved because they are also a way to conceal diverted collections.
scr_ar_writing_off_unpaid_invoices.ifSkipped: A/R is overstated with balances that will never be collected, and bad debt is recognized in lumps later.

scr_ar_quick_payments.purpose: The Quick Payments page for recording many customer payments rapidly — for example a batch of checks from ancillary vendors received in one mail run.
scr_ar_quick_payments.outcome: High-volume receipts entered and applied efficiently.
scr_ar_quick_payments.rootCause: Entering each payment through the full receipt page is slow; quick entry keeps daily receipt processing current so deposits and aging stay accurate.
scr_ar_quick_payments.ifSkipped: Receipts back up, deposits are late and aging overstates what customers owe.
redFlags: Batch totals not matching the deposit

scr_ar_using_the_quick_payments_page_to_.purpose: Procedure for recording payments on the Quick Payments page — customer, amount, reference and invoice application per row.
scr_ar_using_the_quick_payments_page_to_.outcome: A batch of receipts recorded and applied in one session.
scr_ar_using_the_quick_payments_page_to_.rootCause: A consistent procedure ensures each quick-entry row still captures the reference needed to match to the bank deposit.
scr_ar_using_the_quick_payments_page_to_.ifSkipped: Quick-entered receipts lack references and cannot be matched.

scr_ar_deposits.purpose: Explains A/R deposits — grouping customer payments held in Undeposited Funds into a deposit that matches the bank credit.
scr_ar_deposits.outcome: A/R receipts reach the bank account as deposits that reconcile line for line.
scr_ar_deposits.rootCause: The bank shows one credit per deposit; grouping receipts identically makes the bank reconciliation match and exposes missing receipts.
scr_ar_deposits.ifSkipped: Receipts stay in Undeposited Funds and the bank rec cannot be matched.

scr_ar_deposits_workflow.purpose: Diagram of the A/R deposit workflow: payment received into Undeposited Funds, grouped into a deposit, deposited at the bank and cleared in reconciliation.
scr_ar_deposits_workflow.outcome: Users see where a receipt sits at each stage.
scr_ar_deposits_workflow.rootCause: Tracing a missing payment requires knowing whether it was recorded, deposited or cleared; the workflow shows those states.
scr_ar_deposits_workflow.ifSkipped: Missing receipts cannot be traced to where they stopped.

scr_ar_undeposited_funds_accounts.purpose: Configures the undeposited funds account used by A/R to hold checks and cash received but not yet deposited.
scr_ar_undeposited_funds_accounts.outcome: A/R receipts flow through a holding account that exposes undeposited items.
scr_ar_undeposited_funds_accounts.rootCause: Without an undeposited funds step, receipts post straight to cash and the bank rec cannot tell receipts not yet deposited from missing deposits.
scr_ar_undeposited_funds_accounts.ifSkipped: Undeposited receipts are invisible and misappropriation is harder to detect.
redFlags: Undeposited funds mapped to operating cash

scr_ar_deposits_list.purpose: Lists A/R deposits with bank, date, amount and status for review, printing and reversal.
scr_ar_deposits_list.outcome: A deposit register for matching to bank statements.
scr_ar_deposits_list.rootCause: Deposits in transit at month-end are listed on the bank rec from this register; it is also where late deposits show up.
scr_ar_deposits_list.ifSkipped: Deposits in transit cannot be supported.
redFlags: Deposits recorded but not cleared after several days

scr_ar_adding_a_deposit.purpose: Creates an A/R deposit by selecting undeposited customer payments and the bank account and date of deposit.
scr_ar_adding_a_deposit.outcome: Customer receipts move from Undeposited Funds to cash as one deposit matching the bank.
scr_ar_adding_a_deposit.rootCause: Recording the deposit exactly as made (same date, same checks) is what lets the bank rec match one book line to one bank credit.
scr_ar_adding_a_deposit.ifSkipped: Receipts remain undeposited in the books and cash is understated.
redFlags: Deposit dates differing from bank credit dates

scr_ar_viewing_and_verifying_deposits.purpose: Opens an A/R deposit to verify its payments and total against the deposit slip and bank credit.
scr_ar_viewing_and_verifying_deposits.outcome: Deposit discrepancies caught before the bank rec.
scr_ar_viewing_and_verifying_deposits.rootCause: Differences between recorded deposits and bank credits are early signs of keying errors or missing checks.
redFlags: Deposit total not equal to bank credit

scr_ar_printing_deposit_details.purpose: Prints the detail of an A/R deposit — each payment, payer and amount — to accompany the deposit or support the bank rec.
scr_ar_printing_deposit_details.outcome: Evidence of which customer payments made up a deposit.
scr_ar_printing_deposit_details.rootCause: When a customer disputes a payment, the deposit detail links their check to a specific bank credit.
scr_ar_printing_deposit_details.ifSkipped: Customer payment disputes cannot be resolved from bank totals alone.

scr_ar_reversing_deposits.purpose: Explains that A/R deposits are reversed rather than deleted, preserving the cash audit trail.
scr_ar_reversing_deposits.outcome: Deposit corrections always leave a visible record.
scr_ar_reversing_deposits.rootCause: Deleting deposits would allow cash records to change without trace; reversal is the controlled correction.
scr_ar_reversing_deposits.ifSkipped: Deposit history could be altered invisibly.

scr_ar_reversing_a_deposit.purpose: Reverses an A/R deposit recorded to the wrong bank account or date, returning its payments to Undeposited Funds for re-deposit.
scr_ar_reversing_a_deposit.outcome: The erroneous deposit is cancelled and the payments can be deposited correctly.
scr_ar_reversing_a_deposit.rootCause: Deposits recorded to the wrong account break two bank recs; reversal moves them back cleanly.
scr_ar_reversing_a_deposit.ifSkipped: Deposits stay in the wrong account and both recs break.

scr_ar_reversing_a_payment_in_a_deposit.purpose: Reverses one customer payment inside an A/R deposit — usually a returned check — without reversing the whole deposit.
scr_ar_reversing_a_payment_in_a_deposit.outcome: The returned payment is reinstated on the customer's account.
scr_ar_reversing_a_payment_in_a_deposit.rootCause: Returned checks affect single payments; reversing only that payment keeps the rest of the deposit matched to the bank.
scr_ar_reversing_a_payment_in_a_deposit.ifSkipped: Returned payments remain credited and A/R and cash are overstated.

scr_ar_deposit_page.purpose: The page for recording an A/R deposit — bank account, date and selected undeposited payments.
scr_ar_deposit_page.outcome: A deposit that matches the physical deposit.
scr_ar_deposit_page.rootCause: Accurate deposit entry is the book side of deposit matching in the bank reconciliation.
scr_ar_deposit_page.ifSkipped: Receipts remain in Undeposited Funds and the bank rec cannot match.
redFlags: Deposits mixing receipts from different entities

scr_ar_manual_deposits.purpose: Explains manual deposits — recording a customer payment directly to a bank account (e.g., a wire or ACH received) without first going through Undeposited Funds.
scr_ar_manual_deposits.outcome: Electronic receipts recorded directly to the bank account they arrived in.
scr_ar_manual_deposits.rootCause: Wires and ACH credits arrive in the bank before anyone records them; a manual deposit records the receipt against the customer at the same time as the cash.
scr_ar_manual_deposits.ifSkipped: Electronic receipts show as unexplained bank credits and customers look delinquent.

scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_manual_deposi.purpose: Opens the list of manual deposits — customer payments such as wires and ACH credits recorded directly to a bank account without passing through Undeposited Funds.
scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_manual_deposi.outcome: Visibility of electronic receipts recorded directly to cash.
scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_manual_deposi.rootCause: Manual deposits bypass the undeposited funds step, so they deserve separate review for correct customer application.
scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_manual_deposi.ifSkipped: Direct receipts are not reviewed for correct application.

scr_ar_manual_deposits_list.purpose: Lists manual deposits with customer, bank account, date and amount, used to match electronic customer receipts to bank statement credits.
scr_ar_manual_deposits_list.outcome: A register of direct electronic receipts for bank matching.
scr_ar_manual_deposits_list.rootCause: Wires and ACH credits must be matched to bank lines; the list supports that and highlights unapplied amounts.
scr_ar_manual_deposits_list.ifSkipped: Electronic receipts cannot be efficiently matched to the bank.
redFlags: Manual deposits not matching bank credits

scr_ar_adding_a_manual_deposit.purpose: Adds a manual deposit — customer, bank account, date, amount and invoices paid — for a payment received directly in the bank.
scr_ar_adding_a_manual_deposit.outcome: The receipt is recorded to cash and the customer's invoices in one step.
scr_ar_adding_a_manual_deposit.rootCause: Recording wires the same day they arrive keeps customer balances current and the bank rec clean.
scr_ar_adding_a_manual_deposit.ifSkipped: Wires sit as unexplained credits and customers are chased for amounts already paid.
redFlags: Manual deposits dated differently from the bank credit

scr_ar_recording_a_manual_deposit.purpose: Procedure for recording a manual deposit: select the customer and bank account, enter the wire or ACH amount and date, and apply it to the customer's open invoices.
scr_ar_recording_a_manual_deposit.rootCause: A defined procedure ensures manual deposits are applied to invoices, not left on account.
scr_ar_recording_a_manual_deposit.ifSkipped: Manual deposits are recorded but left unapplied.

scr_ar_viewing_a_manual_deposits_details.purpose: Views a manual deposit's details — customer, bank account, date and the invoices it paid — typically to resolve a customer's question about a wired payment.
scr_ar_viewing_a_manual_deposits_details.outcome: Full detail of one direct receipt.
scr_ar_viewing_a_manual_deposits_details.rootCause: Disputes over wired payments are resolved by showing exactly which invoices the wire paid.
scr_ar_viewing_a_manual_deposits_details.ifSkipped: Wire payment disputes are hard to resolve.
redFlags: Wires applied to the wrong customer

scr_ar_manual_deposit_page.purpose: The page showing a manual deposit's full record — customer, bank, reference, amount and invoice applications — for review and audit.
scr_ar_manual_deposit_page.outcome: A complete record of a direct receipt.
scr_ar_manual_deposit_page.rootCause: Direct receipts need the same traceability as regular deposits for audits and bank reconciliation.
scr_ar_manual_deposit_page.ifSkipped: Direct electronic receipts lack traceability for bank recs and audits.

scr_ar_duplicating_a_manual_deposit.purpose: Adds a manual deposit by duplicating an existing one — useful for recurring wires from the same customer.
scr_ar_duplicating_a_manual_deposit.rootCause: Customers who wire monthly (affiliates, cell tower licensees) create repetitive entries; duplicating saves time while keeping coding consistent.
scr_ar_duplicating_a_manual_deposit.ifSkipped: Recurring receipts are keyed from scratch with inconsistent coding.
redFlags: Duplicates left with prior dates or amounts

scr_ar_advances.purpose: Explains advances — prepayments or retainers received from customers before invoicing, recorded as a liability until applied.
scr_ar_advances.outcome: Customer prepayments are held as liabilities, not income.
scr_ar_advances.rootCause: Money received before the service or period it pays for is not yet earned; recognizing it as revenue overstates income and misstates the balance sheet.
scr_ar_advances.ifSkipped: Prepayments are recorded as revenue too early.

scr_ar_receiving_and_recording_a_r_advan.purpose: Receives and records an advance payment from a customer, such as a tenant prepaying three months of rent.
scr_ar_receiving_and_recording_a_r_advan.outcome: The prepayment is recorded as a liability ready to apply to future invoices.
scr_ar_receiving_and_recording_a_r_advan.rootCause: Recording advances properly ensures revenue is recognized in the months it is earned and the customer's prepaid position is tracked.
scr_ar_receiving_and_recording_a_r_advan.ifSkipped: Prepaid amounts are forgotten or recognized too early.

scr_ar_recording_an_advance_payment.purpose: Procedure for recording an advance — customer, amount, date, deposit account and liability account.
scr_ar_recording_an_advance_payment.rootCause: Using the correct liability account for advances keeps prepaid amounts visible on the balance sheet.
scr_ar_recording_an_advance_payment.ifSkipped: Advances post to revenue instead of a liability and income is overstated.

scr_ar_creating_a_deposit_from_an_advanc.purpose: Creates a bank deposit from recorded advance payments so the customer's prepayment moves from Undeposited Funds to the operating account in the books.
scr_ar_creating_a_deposit_from_an_advanc.outcome: Advance receipts reach the bank account in the books.
scr_ar_creating_a_deposit_from_an_advanc.rootCause: Advances are cash received; they must be deposited like other receipts for the bank rec to match.
scr_ar_creating_a_deposit_from_an_advanc.ifSkipped: Advance receipts sit in Undeposited Funds.

scr_ar_receive_advances_page.purpose: The page for receiving advances, with the top section for essentials (customer, amount, date) and lines for allocation.
scr_ar_receive_advances_page.outcome: Advance payments entered with complete header and line detail.
scr_ar_receive_advances_page.rootCause: An advance must carry the customer, amount, reference and allocation so it can be deposited, matched to the bank and applied to the right future invoices.
scr_ar_receive_advances_page.ifSkipped: Advances lack the detail needed for application.

scr_ar_entering_basic_information_about_.purpose: Enters the advance header — customer, date, amount, payment method and reference.
scr_ar_entering_basic_information_about_.rootCause: The reference and date tie the advance to the bank deposit and the customer's records.
scr_ar_entering_basic_information_about_.ifSkipped: Advances cannot be matched to deposits or to the customer's remittance.

scr_ar_entering_line_items_for_the_advan.purpose: Enters the line items of an advance payment, assigning the prepaid amount to liability accounts, properties and dimensions so it can be applied correctly later.
scr_ar_entering_line_items_for_the_advan.outcome: Advances allocated to the correct liability accounts and properties.
scr_ar_entering_line_items_for_the_advan.rootCause: An advance covering several properties or charge types must be split so each is applied correctly later.
scr_ar_entering_line_items_for_the_advan.ifSkipped: Advances are applied to the wrong property or charge.
redFlags: Line totals not equal to advance amount

scr_ar_applying_the_advance_to_the_balan.purpose: Applies a recorded advance to invoices when they are billed, converting the liability into payment of revenue.
scr_ar_applying_the_advance_to_the_balan.outcome: Prepaid amounts settle invoices in the periods they are earned.
scr_ar_applying_the_advance_to_the_balan.rootCause: Advances left unapplied mean the customer looks delinquent while the property holds their money.
scr_ar_applying_the_advance_to_the_balan.ifSkipped: Customers look delinquent and prepaid liabilities are overstated.
redFlags: Advances unapplied while invoices are open

scr_ar_posted_advances_list.purpose: Lists posted customer advances with amount received, amount applied and remaining unapplied balance, showing prepaid money the property is holding for customers.
scr_ar_posted_advances_list.outcome: Visibility of prepaid amounts held for customers.
scr_ar_posted_advances_list.rootCause: Unapplied advances are liabilities that must be applied or refunded; the list shows them.
scr_ar_posted_advances_list.ifSkipped: Unapplied prepayments linger as liabilities and customers look delinquent.

scr_ar_viewing_posted_advance_details.purpose: Views a posted advance's details and each application against invoices, showing how much of the customer's prepayment has been used.
scr_ar_viewing_posted_advance_details.outcome: Clarity on how much of an advance has been used.
scr_ar_viewing_posted_advance_details.rootCause: Customers who prepay rent or fees routinely ask how their money was applied; a clear application history answers them and supports audits of prepaid liabilities.

scr_ar_printing_posted_payment_informati.purpose: Prints posted advance or payment information — amount received and how it was applied — to send to the customer as confirmation or keep in the file.
scr_ar_printing_posted_payment_informati.rootCause: Customers who prepay often want confirmation; printed records also support audits of liabilities.
redFlags: Confirmations sent before the advance cleared the bank

scr_ar_reversing_an_advance.purpose: Reverses an advance that was misapplied to the wrong customer or returned by the bank, removing the prepaid liability and the cash receipt with an audit trail.
scr_ar_reversing_an_advance.outcome: Incorrect advances removed with an audit trail.
scr_ar_reversing_an_advance.rootCause: Advances recorded to the wrong customer or returned by the bank must be reversed to keep liabilities and cash correct.
scr_ar_reversing_an_advance.ifSkipped: Prepaid liabilities and cash are misstated.

scr_ar_posted_advance_page.purpose: The record page for a posted advance showing amounts, applications and remaining balance.
scr_ar_posted_advance_page.outcome: A complete record of one customer prepayment.
scr_ar_posted_advance_page.rootCause: Tracking prepayment use over time requires a single record showing remaining balance.

scr_ar_printing_posted_advance_details.purpose: Prints the details of a posted advance, including applications and remaining balance, for customer confirmation or audit support of prepaid liabilities.
scr_ar_printing_posted_advance_details.outcome: A printed record of the advance's use.
scr_ar_printing_posted_advance_details.rootCause: Printed advance details support customer questions and audit testing of prepaid liabilities.
scr_ar_printing_posted_advance_details.ifSkipped: Advance support is unavailable when requested.

scr_ar_adjustments.purpose: Explains A/R adjustments — credit and debit adjustments to a customer's account for corrections, concessions and small write-offs, plus editing, exporting and importing them.
scr_ar_adjustments.outcome: Customer balances corrected through documented adjustments.
scr_ar_adjustments.rootCause: Balances drift from what is owed because of billing errors and negotiated settlements; adjustments correct them without altering original invoices.
scr_ar_adjustments.ifSkipped: Customer balances stay wrong or are corrected by untraceable JEs.
redFlags: Frequent credits to the same customer

scr_ar_viewing_a_list_of_a_r_adjustments.purpose: Views the list of A/R credit and debit adjustments with customer, type, amount, reason and user, as the basis for reviewing customer credits each month.
scr_ar_viewing_a_list_of_a_r_adjustments.outcome: Visibility of all credits and debits applied to customers.
scr_ar_viewing_a_list_of_a_r_adjustments.rootCause: Credits reduce revenue and receivables; reviewing them as a list is a key fraud and error control.
scr_ar_viewing_a_list_of_a_r_adjustments.ifSkipped: Unauthorized or unsupported credits go unnoticed.

scr_ar_adjustments_list.purpose: The Adjustments list under Account Maintenance with actions to add, view, edit and export adjustments.
scr_ar_adjustments_list.outcome: A managed register of customer adjustments.
scr_ar_adjustments_list.rootCause: Monthly review of adjustments by someone independent of collections deters and detects improper credits.
scr_ar_adjustments_list.ifSkipped: Customer credits escape independent review, weakening fraud controls.
redFlags: Adjustments entered by staff who also receive payments

scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_credit_adjustment.purpose: Adds a credit adjustment reducing a customer's balance — for a billing correction, approved concession or small write-off — saved as draft or posted.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_credit_adjustment.outcome: The customer's balance is reduced with a documented reason and GL offset.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_credit_adjustment.rootCause: Credits must carry a reason and the correct offset (concessions vs bad debt vs revenue correction) so revenue analysis and the allowance stay accurate.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_credit_adjustment.ifSkipped: Balances stay overstated or credits are coded to the wrong accounts.
redFlags: Credits coded to revenue accounts instead of concessions

scr_ar_creating_a_debit_adjustment.purpose: Creates a debit adjustment increasing a customer's balance — for a missed charge or a reversal of a prior credit.
scr_ar_creating_a_debit_adjustment.outcome: Missed charges are added to the customer's account.
scr_ar_creating_a_debit_adjustment.rootCause: Charges missed in billing (e.g., a CAM true-up) must be added with a documented basis to be collectible.
scr_ar_creating_a_debit_adjustment.ifSkipped: Revenue from missed or under-billed charges is never collected.

scr_ar_editing_an_a_r_adjustment.purpose: Edits a draft A/R adjustment — amount, reason, offset account — before it is posted to the customer's account and the GL.
scr_ar_editing_an_a_r_adjustment.outcome: Adjustment details corrected before affecting the GL.
scr_ar_editing_an_a_r_adjustment.rootCause: Correcting an adjustment while it is a draft avoids posting and then reversing it, keeping the customer ledger and audit trail clean.
scr_ar_editing_an_a_r_adjustment.ifSkipped: Wrong adjustments are posted and must be reversed.

scr_ar_viewing_a_r_adjustment_details.purpose: Views an A/R adjustment's details — customer, type, amount, reason and GL distribution.
scr_ar_viewing_a_r_adjustment_details.outcome: Full detail of one adjustment for review.
scr_ar_viewing_a_r_adjustment_details.rootCause: Reviewers must see the reason and offset account to judge whether an adjustment was appropriate.

scr_ar_importing_a_r_adjustments.purpose: Imports A/R adjustments in bulk from a template — for example opening balance adjustments at onboarding or a batch of approved write-offs.
scr_ar_importing_a_r_adjustments.rootCause: Onboarding and periodic cleanups involve many adjustments; importing ensures consistency and a clear batch record.
scr_ar_importing_a_r_adjustments.ifSkipped: Adjustments are keyed manually with errors.
